title: Warning icons
intro: Final D31: gold is for rating stars only. Warning indicators use dark icon/action on subtle or solid Warning surfaces.
caveat: Both dark Warning pairings are approved under D31. Gold samples remain historical comparisons only. Example container geometry is illustrative; whole-component accessibility still needs native validation.

cards.title: Gold on neutral
cards.note: Historical comparison only. Final D31 prohibits gold Warning glyphs; icon/warning is rating-stars-only.

cards.title: Gold on warning tint
cards.note: Historical comparison only. Final D31 prohibits gold Warning glyphs; icon/warning is rating-stars-only.

cards.title: Dark icon on warning tint
cards.note: Final D31 recipe across toast, input and icon badge. Neutral toast/input outer surfaces remain unchanged; container geometry is still open.

cards.title: Dark icon on solid Warning
cards.note: Second approved Warning indicator recipe. Use only where the component specifies a solid Warning surface, not as permission to recolour the entire toast/input.

title: Resting input boundaries
intro: Keep the field fill, dimensions and text identical. Only the boundary colour varies.
caveat: The 3:1 comparison applies when the boundary is necessary to identify the control. An otherwise clearly identifiable input may have a decorative border. Determine whether the complete field can be recognised without this line; a darkened stroke is a proposal, not an automatic requirement.

cards.title: Current subtle boundary
cards.note: The existing rest border. Labels and other cues matter when assessing the complete field.

cards.title: Existing strong stroke
cards.note: Reuses an existing stroke role, with noticeably stronger visual weight. Input adoption is not approved.

cards.title: Middle neutral candidate
cards.note: A palette candidate only. No semantic rest-border token exists for this mapping; token and component approval would be required.

title: Brand text on the pressed fill
intro: Compare the current Secondary/Tertiary pressed label against two alternatives. The default reading-text threshold is 4.5:1.
caveat: The current state is transient, but that alone is not a blanket WCAG exemption for active text. Large text has a different threshold; these 16 pt semibold samples are evaluated conservatively at 4.5:1. A proposed primitive is not an approved semantic text token.

cards.title: Current brand label
cards.note: Current pressed Secondary/Tertiary recipe; retained in the skills pending review.

cards.title: Existing default text
cards.note: Uses an existing text role and the same pressed fill. This changes brand emphasis and needs shared design approval.

cards.title: Deeper brand candidate
cards.note: Keeps a brand hue but requires a semantic text mapping. It is not a new token or an approved replacement.

title: Text on a dark brand surface
intro: This case already has a safe rule in D26: use text/inverse. It is included so an already settled restriction is not mistaken for a new proposal.
caveat: D26 prohibits brand and subtle text on dark surfaces. Existing approved inverse text can be used now; it does not need another colour decision.

cards.title: Brand text on dark
cards.note: Included to illustrate the restricted pairing, not as a permitted implementation.

cards.title: Inverse text on dark
cards.note: Existing D26 rule. Keep this mapping on bg/brand/bold and bg/inverse.
